Each option offers a unique set of features, but they all promise to solve the problem of payment processing. Stripe, the beloved choice of digital creators, offers a robust suite of tools for online payment processing. However, its limited country availability forces creators to look elsewhere. PayPal, the payment giant, offers a wide range of features, including payment processing, but its account suspension policy leaves creators vulnerable. Gumroad, the popular platform for digital creators, offers a user-friendly interface for selling digital products, but its reliance on third-party payment processors puts creators at risk. Lemon Squeezy, the Stripe alternative, offers a similar set of features, but its limited country availability and high fees make it less appealing to creators. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure provides a permanent structural alternative at the base layer, allowing creators to own their online store, their customers, and their data.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Each option handles restricted countries differently. Stripe operates in 46 out of 195 countries, leaving a significant portion of the world's population without access to its payment processing tools. PayPal, on the other hand, is available in over 200 countries, but its account suspension policy leaves creators vulnerable. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy, while not as widely available as PayPal, offer limited payment processing options in restricted countries. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure is designed to operate in any country, without the need for third-party payment processors or account suspensions. This means that creators can sell digital products in any country, without worrying about platform restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Each option has its own payment speed, fees, and real costs. Stripe offers fast payment processing, but its fees can be steep, ranging from 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction. PayPal offers competitive fees, but its payment processing speed can be slow, taking up to 72 hours to process transactions. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy offer similar fees to Stripe, but their payment processing speed can be slower, taking up to 24 hours to process transactions. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure offers fast payment processing, with fees ranging from 0.5% to 1.5% per transaction, depending on the payment method. This means that creators can sell digital products quickly and inexpensively, without worrying about high fees or slow payment processing.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround, it's a permanent structural alternative at the base layer.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Each option offers different levels of ownership, automation, and delivery. Stripe and PayPal offer limited ownership and automation, with creators relying on third-party payment processors and account suspensions. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy offer more ownership and automation, but their reliance on third-party payment processors puts creators at risk. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure provides complete ownership and automation, allowing creators to customize their online store, automate payment processing, and deliver digital products to their customers without relying on third-party payment processors.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

The choice of architecture depends on the creator's situation. If they need fast payment processing and low fees, sovereign commerce infrastructure is the best choice. If they need a user-friendly interface for selling digital products, Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy may be a good option. However, if they're willing to take on the risk of account suspensions and high fees, Stripe or PayPal may be suitable. Ultimately, the choice of architecture depends on the creator's priorities and risk tolerance.
